hypothesis: Variable-density LBM equilibrium f_i^eq = w_i * rho(C) * [1 + 3(e_i.u) + 9/2(e_i.u)^2 - 3/2(u.u)] with rho(C) = rho_L + C*(rho_H - rho_L) recovers the analytic layered Poiseuille profile for two immiscible fluids of different density within <15% error.
decision: Whether the linear-in-C density mapping in the equilibrium distribution correctly reproduces the physics of variable-density Poiseuille flow.
alternatives: A1: variable-density equilibrium (rho depends on C linearly)
A3: analytic layered Poiseuille solution (physical anchor)
metrics: L2 relative error of velocity profile vs analytic
Max relative error of velocity profile vs analytic
stopping_rule: Run until steady state: max|u(n) - u(n-200)| / max|u(n)| < 1e-9, or 50000 steps cap.
confounders: Mach number must be < 0.1 to ensure incompressible limit
Interface must be sharp (no diffusion of C)
Viscosity must be matched or accounted for in analytic solution
Body force must be scaled by local density for correct physics
repetition_rationale: Single run per case; deterministic LBM with fixed seed. Resolution sensitivity tested at two grid sizes.
analysis: Compare LBM velocity profile against analytic layered Poiseuille solution. L2 and max relative errors computed over fluid nodes only.
external_anchor: Walberla PhaseField Allen-Cahn multiphase (lssfau/walberla, apps/showcases/PhaseFieldAllenCahn/CPU/multiphase_codegen.py); Krüger et al. 'The Lattice Boltzmann Method' (2017), Ch. 9 on multiphase/multicomponent LBM.
